- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently over-optimistic; apply downward bias of 3–7% to avoid “bullish overfitting.”
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model exhibits high variance; use 30-day moving average as baseline and adjust by ±1–2% based on sentiment directionality.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward sentiment; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment remains flat or mildly negative for >5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if price deviates >3σ from 30-day mean, apply correction toward mean with decay factor (e.g., 0.85 per day).
